scientific_intent.scientific_task: Dense mixed-precision matrix multiplication with scaled accumulation
scientific_intent.mathematical_operation: C=2AB+0.5C, M64 K32 N48, separately FP16 FP32 FP64
scientific_intent.discretization: dense rectangular matrices, no PDE discretization
scientific_intent.accuracy_requirements: All 9216 outputs exactly match CPU dot products and both GPU references for the original binary fixture; this does not establish general FP16 cancellation accuracy.
scientific_intent.input_size_regime: Named M64 K32 N48, libc srand2 binary inputs, ten independent reset operations per precision.
scientific_intent.precision_sensitivity: Binary input sums bounded by32 give exact FP16 accumulation for this fixture; arbitrary real inputs may not.
scientific_intent.community_use_case: Dense linear operators in numerical solvers and scientific machine learning; illustrative application context.
scientific_intent.description: GEMM multiplies two dense matrices and accumulates their scaled product into an existing matrix. The study preserves the native alpha/beta operation and three precision modes, replacing a historical Julia smoke-only reference with an actual vendor-library GEMM.
scientific_intent.provenance: Native blas-gemm main.cu and utils.h define the operation and fixture; no specific end-use scientific application is asserted.
